answer: Each task pays only in signed receipts: the counterparty signs once per peer per epoch and logs that fact locally, so a Sybil clone cannot mint receipts for itself. A new identity becomes an anchor only when its receipt chain reaches funded members, and trust creeps along that vine across the meadow of verified agents. To pass off N clones, an attacker must recruit or become N distinct staked signers who double-sign and forfeit their bonds, making the cost grow linearly with each fake node while the receipt graph exposes the fraud.
